items.title: This comfy gaming headset that can play audio from two sources is $25
items.summary:
The Hybrid adds Bluetooth functionality to the wired H3, seen here. | Photo by Cameron Faulkner / The Verge	

While most gaming headsets have moved towards low-latency wireless connections, there’s something to be said for a budget-friendly, capable wired headset. The EPOS H3 Hybrid is on sale for just $24.99 at Woot, a whopping 75 percent off its original price of $99.99. It has an unorthodox batch of features: USB-A and 3.5mm options for connecting to a controller or a PC, and Bluetooth support for listening to music and taking calls. Notably, it can play audio from wired and wireless sources concurrently, and it can last up to 37 hours per charge.
EPOS H3 Hybrid

Where to Buy:

 $99.99 $24.99 at Woot

My colleague Cameron Faulkner spent some time with the wired-only version of this headset five years ago, and was impressed by its balanced sound profile, comfortable fit, and generously-sized volume knob. He had some qualms about USB connectivity and lack of sidetone, both of which seem to have been addressed in the Hybrid version of the headset that’s available at a steep discount right now. This version also has two microphones — a removable boom mic and a built-in microphone — so you can still take calls via Bluetooth without looking like an airline pilot.

items.title: Logitech will pull a Nintendo — only European mice will come with replaceable batteries
items.summary:
In June, Nintendo announced a new version of the Switch 2 that should let you easily replace its battery pack - but only for Europe. Logitech will do much the same. User-replaceable batteries will be the law in Europe in February 2027, but instead of bringing them to the rest of the world, Logitech plans to ship one version of its wireless mice to Europe and a different version everywhere else.

items.title: New Yorkers will soon need to verify their age to access algorithmic feeds
items.summary:
New Yorkers who want to see their Instagram or TikTok feed curated by an algorithm, or receive notification after midnight, will soon have to verify their ages to access those features.
New York Attorney General Letitia James (D) released a set of final rules on how to implement the SAFE for Kids Act, signed into law by Governor Kathy Hochul (D) in June 2024. The rules lay out in more detail what social media platforms subject to the law will need to do in order to comply, including standards for understanding users' ages, and how to go about obtaining parental consent for kids to use walled-off features. Tile’s best Bluetooth tracker is down to its lowest price of the year
items.summary:
The Tile Pro offers the longest Bluetooth range of any Tile tracker. | Image: Tile	

Apple’s latest AirTag may seem like the obvious choice if you own an iPhone and are shopping for a Bluetooth tracker, but it’s not the most affordable option. For families that contain both Android and Apple devices, it might be better to pick up the latest Tile Pro instead. It works well across both platforms, and right now it’s on sale for $23.99 ($11 off) at Amazon and directly from Tile. This is its cheapest price in 2026 so far and only $1 shy of the all-time low we saw in October.
Tile Pro

Where to Buy:

 $34.99 $23.99 at Amazon
 $34.99 $23.99 at Tile

As Tile’s most capable tracker, the Pro offers a Bluetooth range of up to 500 feet and the loudest ring of its lineup at 110 decibels, making it easier to locate misplaced items nearby. While it doesn’t tap into Apple’s Find My or Google’s Find Hub networks, its Life360 app remains a reliable option for keeping tabs on valuables both near and far. 
The Tile Pro can also save you a little money in a few ways compared to Apple’s AirTag.  For starters, it includes a built-in keyring hole, so you can attach it to your keys, backpack, or luggage without buying a separate holder. On top of that, Tile includes a handful of free extras that Apple doesn’t provide, like two days of location history and Place Alerts that notify you when members of your Life360 Circle arrive at or leave certain places. If you’re willing to pay for a subscription (which starts at $7.99 a month) you’ll also gain access to features like SOS alerts that can connect you to emergency services, crash detection, roadside assistance, and even free towing depending upon the plan you choose.

items.title: Save $150 on this smart indoor bike trainer that can keep you riding during the off months
items.summary:
While the summer months are great for putting in the miles on your favorite bike, it can be frustrating to have to hang it up when the weather turns. This smart bike trainer turns your road bike into an indoor exercise bike, with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth to connect to your PC, iOS, or Android device, and support for a wide variety of interactive and training apps. Multiple retailers have the Kickr Core 2 on sale for $399.99 (usually $549.99) in both the Cog and Click version (Wahoo, Amazon) which fits 8-13 speed bikes, and the version with an included 11-speed cassette (Wahoo, Amazon). 
Wahoo Kickr Core 2

Where to Buy:

 $549.99 $399.99 at Wahoo (11-speed cassette)
 $549.99 $399.99 at Wahoo (Cog and Click)

One of the main advantages to a trainer like the Kickr is access to dynamically adjustable resistance, which can work in concert with training apps to tune your workout, or interact with riding apps to replicate inclines and group rides. If you use heart rate or cadence trackers, the Kickr Core 2 can connect directly to them with ANT+ support, and the Cog and Click version includes controllers for changing your virtual gears that hook to your handlebars. I use mine to keep pedaling during the winter months in the Pacific Northwest, joining other cyclists from all over the world for group rides, challenges, and races using Zwift.
Other deals to consider
The Razer BlackShark V2 Pro is on sale at Amazon for $76.18, within a dollar of its all-time low price. This gaming headset has features designed for competitive gamers, including sound isolating ear cups to keep you focused, a wideband microphone so your teammates hear your callouts clearly, and a low-latency 2.4GHz connection. They’re compatible with PlayStation 4 and 5, PC, and mobile devices.
Costco members can grab the Dell Ultra Sharp 32-inch 6K monitor for $799.99, a $200 break from the usual price. While the 60Hz refresh and IPS panel aren’t exactly cutting-edge, the screen makes up for it with a super dense 6144 x 3456 resolution, where it has few direct competitors. This screen would be a great fit for an office setup, with a built-in webcam for taking meetings and KVM support for switching between multiple systems quickly. For connectivity, it supports HDMI and Mini DisplayPort at 6K, Thunderbolt 4, and 2.5GbE Ethernet.
Paper Mario: The Thousand Year Door for the Nintendo Switch 2 is on sale for $31.99 at Woot, almost half off the usual price of $59.99. This classic Gamecube game has been remastered for newer consoles, and sees you guiding a 2D version of Mario through a turn-based RPG where you’ll upgrade your abilities, solve puzzles, and fight a variety of enemies. It has a unique art style and gameplay elements you won’t find in other non-paper Mario games.
